checks.name: one-new-member-interface-on-ports
checks.summary: internal/application/ports.go gains exactly one member interface, RepositoryRepository (Repository, Repositories, SaveRepository, RepositoryObservation, SaveRepositoryObservation), plus one line adding it to UnitOfWork. No existing port method signature changed. The Observation lives on the same member interface rather than behind a second port because it is keyed by, and only meaningful for, a Repository -- the same shape RunnerObservationRepository already has. Adding the member forces both store adapters to implement it in the same change, which is the intended coupling (dp-v2-064 risk 3): only internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore implement UnitOfWork, verified by grep; the four other Transact implementations in tests are Transactor wrappers, not UnitOfWork implementations.

checks.name: capture-pattern-followed-for-the-three-mutations
checks.summary: RegisterRepository, RetireRepository and ObserveRepository each mirror Service.Capture (service.go L581-651) step for step: callerActor role check, requestedBy for attribution, requireRequest on RequestID, requestFingerprint for idempotency, s.ids.Next for the identifier, s.mutate keyed by operation and request id, an Idempotency read that replays a matching fingerprint and returns ErrIdempotencyConflict on a differing one, a domain.Permit gate on domain.PermitIntake with ControlTarget{InstallationID, RepositoryID}, validation through domain.ValidateRepository, and one s.record event. Asserted: 401-class ErrUnauthenticated without a caller, ErrForbidden for the wrong role on all five operations, refusal of a missing request id, replay equality on a repeated request id, and ErrIdempotencyConflict on a differing fingerprint for the same request id.

checks.name: read-operations-deviate-from-the-capture-pattern-deliberately
checks.summary: Measured deviation from A5, recorded rather than silently taken: ListRepositories and GetRepository do NOT carry the mutation ceremony. A read has no request body, so it has no request_id to be idempotent on; running s.mutate for a read would reserve quota.MutationUsage against the Installation's bounded daily Firestore budget and would write an idempotency record for an operation that changes nothing. Both follow the house read pattern instead -- callerActor plus s.transact -- exactly as Service.GetRequirementDetail and Service.QueueSummary do. The reason is stated in the file's own header comment. Everything in A5 that a read can carry (the callerActor role check, and validation) is carried.

checks.name: duplicate-locator-constraint
checks.summary: Five spellings of one already-registered repository are each refused with ErrRepositoryAlreadyRegistered, and the list is then asserted to still hold exactly one Repository, so a refusal creates no second record. A different repository on the same forge is not a duplicate. Uniqueness is enforced on the normalised (forge, owner, name) triple; the raw URL is never stored and never used as a key.

checks.name: retire-is-the-rollback
checks.summary: A12 with two registered Repositories: retiring one moves registered->retired through DecideRepository, bumps its version by exactly one, and leaves the other's stored record identical in version, status and locator. The retired Repository is excluded from the list but still readable, so the rollback is observable rather than a disappearance. Retire is idempotent by request id; a second retire is ErrInvalidTransition; retiring an unknown id is ErrNotFound. Retiring frees the locator, so the coordinate can be registered again -- the Installation really is back in its pre-registration state for it. The aggregate is never deleted.

checks.name: installation-owned-not-person-owned
checks.summary: A7: a Repository registered by owner subject "owner-one" is visible in the list to a different authenticated owner caller "owner-two", with the attribution preserved. No per-person filter exists on any view. The stored record is read back through the UnitOfWork and carries no runner identifier under any field; RequestedBy is attribution only and is never interpreted, authenticated or authorized.

checks.name: registration-mutates-nothing-external
checks.summary: A11, proved by construction rather than by inspection. (1) The Service that performs registration is constructed from a Transactor, a Clock and an IDGenerator and nothing else, so it holds no forge client and has no seam through which it could reach GitHub, create a branch, ref or PR, or read a credential. (2) The exported Requirement and Control metadata is byte-count-identical before and after registration, so no existing Application record changed; the single new export row is this task's own repository.registered event. (3) The outbox is the only path by which this codebase performs an external effect, and registration is asserted to stage zero outbox items. The structural half of the same claim (no exec.Command anywhere in the Control Plane) is asserted from the AST in internal/api/repositories_test.go.

checks.name: control-gate-on-the-repository-scoped-target
checks.summary: A repository-scoped Control Intent (domain.ScopeRepository naming the repository id) denies both RetireRepository and ObserveRepository with domain.ErrControlDenied, and the detail view then reports the Repository as blocked with the measured reason and the effective mode. This is the first call site in the codebase where ControlTarget.RepositoryID is non-empty, which is what makes a ScopeRepository Intent match at all.

checks.name: a6-serviceconfig-repositoryid-debt-recorded-not-repaired
checks.summary: Measured and recorded, deliberately NOT repaired (A6, dp-v2-064 d14). application.ServiceConfig has a RepositoryID field at internal/application/service.go L135. It is consumed at L434, L734 and L1088 to build domain.ControlTarget. cmd/control-plane/main.go L172 constructs ServiceConfig with InstallationID and LeaseTTL only, leaving RepositoryID at the zero value, so ControlTarget.RepositoryID is the empty string on every existing production path. domain.matches (internal/domain/control.go L138) compares target.RepositoryID against the scope value, so a domain.ScopeRepository Control Intent -- declared at control.go L26 and accepted by the API at service.go L82 -- can never match anything in production. This task changed none of those three call sites and added no RepositoryID to the ServiceConfig construction. The debt is owned by the successor stage-2 task (dp-v2-064 d1 proposes V2-071; the id is the coordinator's to confirm), because fixing it means changing target construction on the fence-bound Heartbeat, Prepare and AcceptResult paths, which belongs with the Increment-to-Repository link that gives those paths a repository to name. Registration is what finally makes a repository id exist to be named, which is why the debt becomes actionable here. Note: this task's own repositoryTarget() supplies a real repository id and is unaffected by the defect.
